The fast heart rate is a result of the high metabolic rate, not its cause, so the Reason does not explain the Assertion.

questions.text: In an area, a population with large size individuals having long life span, more parental care and slow development was present. The type of population growth curve will be
questions.solution:
Large size, long life span, parental care and slow development are features of species that live close to the carrying capacity of their environment (K-selected species).

Such populations grow logistically, giving an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve with lag, acceleration, exponential, deceleration and stationary phases; most organisms, including humans, show this curve.

The J-shaped curve is unchecked exponential growth.

questions.text: The plants which can withstand with narrow and broad range of temperature tolerance respectively are
questions.solution:

questions.text: Desert can be converted into a lush green land by planting
questions.solution:
Psammophytes are plants that grow readily on sand and gravel, so planting them can cover a sandy desert and turn it into green land.

Xerophytes are adapted to survive scarcity of water, halophytes grow on saline soil, and "terrestrial plants" is a general term for land plants.

questions.text: Resemblance of one organism to another for protection and hiding is
questions.solution:
Mimicry is the resemblance of one organism (the mimic) to another organism (the model), which protects it from predators or hides it from its prey; e.g. palatable butterflies that look like the distasteful Monarch.

Camouflage is resemblance to the surroundings rather than to another organism, predation is one animal feeding on another, and adaptation is a general term for any such feature.

questions.text:
Assertion : Allelopathy is a form of amensalism that occurs in plants.

Reason : Association of rooting plants with fungal hyphae is an important example of amensalism.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and reason is correct explanation of Assertion

questions.text:

questions.text: Sinking of zooplankton during the day and rising to the surface at night is an example of
questions.solution:
Zooplankton move down to deeper water by day and up to the surface at night (diel vertical migration). The movement repeats once in every 24 hours, so it is a circadian (diurnal) rhythm, governed by a biological clock and set by the day–night cycle.

A tidal rhythm follows the tides (about every 12.4 h), not the day–night cycle.

questions.text:
Assertion : Mechanical tissues are absent or less developed in the floating and submerged parts of hydrophytic plants.

Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
questions.solution:
Assertion is true: the surrounding water buoys up floating and submerged parts and shields them from physical injury, so mechanical tissues are absent or poorly developed.

Reason is true: their bodies are made largely of elongated, loosely arranged, thin-walled spongy cells, and these cells, when turgid, give the plant the mechanical support it needs.

Because turgid spongy tissue provides the support, special mechanical tissue is not needed, so the Reason explains the Assertion.

questions.text:
Assertion : Inhibition of death of one organism by another through the production of some by-products is known as antibiosis.

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
questions.solution:
Assertion is true (as intended, "inhibition or death"): antibiosis is the complete or partial inhibition, or the death, of one organism caused by substances produced by another, e.g. antibiotics made by fungi act against bacteria.

Reason is true: in a negative interaction one or both organisms are harmed, and in antibiosis one is harmed while the other gains nothing.

The Reason only classifies antibiosis; it does not explain the inhibition, so it is not the explanation of the Assertion.

questions.text:

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

Assertion is true: submerged hydrophytes absorb water and nutrients over their whole surface directly from the surrounding water, so conducting tissues are poorly developed, xylem most of all; in some the xylem elements do not develop at all.

Reason is false: hydrophytes still have and need tissues; only the need to conduct water from roots is reduced.

questions.text: Which one of the following correctly represents an organism and its ecological niche?
questions.solution:

A pond for Vallisneria, the desert for the desert locust and a dense forest for vultures are habitats, not niches.

questions.text: The great barrier reef along the east coast of Australia can be categorised as :
questions.solution:
A population is a group of individuals of one species in an area, and a community is all the populations of different species living together in that area.

An ecosystem is a community together with its non-living (abiotic) surroundings, while a biome is a very large ecological unit whose organisms are shaped by a particular climatic zone.

The Great Barrier Reef off north-eastern Australia is a vast system of coral reefs, more than 2000 km long and up to about 150 km from the shore, built up as coral polyps keep budding into huge masses. On this scale the book classes it as a biome.

questions.text: Biotic potential or potential natality means

species of maximum number in a population

questions.text: Zero growth means
questions.solution:
Population growth is ΔN=(−)+(−) . Zero growth means no net change in size, which happens when natality balances mortality.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Factor govering the earth surface is
questions.solution:
Topographic factors (altitude, slope and aspect of the land) govern the nature of the earth's surface. Edaphic factors relate to the soil, and biotic factors to living organisms.

questions.text: Predation and parasitism are which type of interactions.
questions.solution:

questions.text: Benthic organisms are found in
questions.solution:
Benthic organisms (benthos) live on or in the bottom of a water body such as the sea floor. Surface dwellers are neuston and organisms in the middle water are nekton or plankton.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: The permanent decrease in population number occurs due to
questions.solution:
Population density increases by natality and immigration and decreases by mortality and emigration.

Mortality is the loss of individuals by death. A dead individual can never rejoin the population, so the decrease caused by mortality is permanent.

Emigrated individuals are still alive and can be regained by immigration, and migration is a periodic movement with return, so neither causes a permanent loss.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Small fish get stuck near the bottom of a shark and derives its nutrition from it. This kind of association is called as
questions.solution:
The sucker fish attaches to the shark and feeds on its leftovers. The fish benefits while the shark is neither harmed nor benefited, which is commensalism.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Animals undergoes inactive stage during winter, is known as
questions.solution:
Winter dormancy of an animal, with greatly reduced metabolism, is hibernation. Aestivation is dormancy in summer.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Animals having a built in thermostat to maintain constant body temperature are known as
questions.solution:
Animals such as birds and mammals maintain a constant body temperature irrespective of the environment, by thermoregulation. They are homeothermic (regulators), whereas poikilotherms change their body temperature with the surroundings.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Study of Ecology of population is called
questions.solution:
Autecology studies a single species, synecology a community, and demecology the ecology of populations.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Which one of the following pairs is mismatched?
questions.solution:
Savanna has scattered Acacia trees, tundra has permanently frozen soil (permafrost), and coniferous forest has evergreen trees.

A prairie is a temperate grassland dominated by grasses with few trees, and epiphytes are characteristic of tropical rainforests. Hence the pair prairie-epiphytes is mismatched.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: The plant that is characteristics component of mangrove vegetation :
questions.solution:
Mangrove vegetation grows in saline coastal swamps and has stilt roots and pneumatophores.

Rhizophora mangle is a characteristic mangrove plant. Ficus religiosa , Mangifera indica and Prosopis are not mangroves.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Biotic factors are :
options: chemical factors of soil which affect life
physical factors of soil which affect life
all living organisms which influence other organisms
questions.solution:
Biotic factors are the living components of the environment, such as plants, animals and microbes, which influence other organisms through interactions like predation, competition and parasitism.

Chemical and physical soil factors are edaphic, and atmospheric factors are climatic (abiotic).

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: On high mountains, difficulty in breathing is due to :
questions.solution:
At high altitude, the percentage of oxygen in air stays about 21 percent, but the atmospheric pressure falls. Hence the partial pressure of oxygen decreases, and the haemoglobin saturation is lower, causing difficulty in breathing (altitude sickness).

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Plants growing on sand and gravel are called
questions.solution:
Plants are named by habitat. Psammophytes grow on sand and gravel. Eremophytes are desert plants and oxylophytes grow on acidic soils.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: The part of earth in which life exist is known as ?
questions.solution:
The biosphere is the zone of the earth where life exists, comprising the lower atmosphere, the hydrosphere and the upper lithosphere. Each of the other options is only one part of it.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: The Orobanche plant is
questions.solution:
Orobanche (broomrape) has no chlorophyll and draws water and food entirely through haustoria from the roots of host plants such as mustard and tobacco. It is therefore a total root parasite.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: The effect of intraspecific competition on niches is to make them
questions.solution:
When members of the same species compete for limited resources, individuals are driven to use a wider range of resources, so the niche of the population widens (niche expansion). It is interspecific competition that narrows (restricts) the niche.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Cattle or goats are never seen browsing on the weed, Calotropis. Select the correct option for the reason.
options: The plant produces quinine, which is bitter in taste.
The plant produces the poisonous chemical, cardiac glycoside.
questions.solution:
Plants protect themselves from herbivores with chemical defences. Calotropis produces highly poisonous cardiac glycosides, which is why cattle and goats avoid it.

Quinine is produced by Cinchona, and the tannins of the plant and prickles are not the reason for the avoidance of Calotropis.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
If a new habitat is being colonized, out of the four processes affecting population growth, which are the two factors that contribute to an increase in population density ?

(i) Immigration

(ii) Natality

(iii) Emigration

(iv) Mortality

Options :
questions.solution:
Population density changes as Nt+1=Nt+[(B+I)−(D+E)] . Natality ( B ) and immigration ( I ) add individuals and so increase density, while mortality ( D ) and emigration ( E ) decrease it. In a newly colonised habitat the increase comes from natality and immigration, i.e. (i) and (ii).

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: In spite of interspecific competition in nature, which of the following mechanisms might competing species have evolved to coexist and survive ?
questions.solution:
Closely related species competing for the same resources may evolve differences in their feeding times or habits, so that each uses the resources differently. This resource partitioning (as in MacArthur's warblers) permits coexistence, whereas competitive exclusion eliminates one species and competitive release is the expansion of a species when its competitor is removed.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which type of interaction is being shown in the figure given below ?
questions.solution:
The figure shows a fish swallowing a frog: one organism (the fish, the predator) kills and eats another organism (the frog, the prey).

In this interaction the predator benefits (+) and the prey is harmed (−) , which is predation.

A parasite lives on or in its host and obtains nourishment from it without eating it whole, commensalism benefits one species with the other unaffected (+/0) , and amensalism harms one species with the other unaffected (−/0) .

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: What could be the reason of extinction of Abingdon Tortoise from Galapagos Islands ?
questions.solution:
On the Galapagos island of Abingdon, goats were introduced. They grazed the vegetation on which the tortoise fed, and the tortoise became extinct within a decade. Goats and tortoises are different species competing for the same food, so the cause is interspecific competition.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Which of the following is an important parameter for assessing the impact of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth ?
questions.solution:
The intrinsic rate of natural increase ( r ) is the difference between per capita birth rate and death rate of a population under ideal conditions. It integrates both natality and mortality, so any biotic or abiotic factor that alters either is reflected as a change in r . Hence r is the parameter used to assess the impact of a factor on population growth.

Birth rate and death rate individually express only one side of the change, and K is the upper limit that the environment can support, not a measure of the growth rate.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Connell’s elegant field experiments on the rocky seacoast of Scotland, found that larger barnacles Balanus dominated the intertidal area and removed the smaller barnacles Chathamalus. This happened due to :
questions.solution:
In Connell's experiments, the larger barnacle Balanus excluded the smaller Chthamalus from the lower intertidal zone because both competed for the same resources, space and food. This interaction is competition.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : The interaction between a whale and the small barnacles on its back is considered as commensalism.

Reason (R) : In the above association, neither of the species is benefitted.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
In the association between a whale and the barnacles growing on its back, the barnacles gain a surface for attachment and are carried to water rich in food, while the whale is neither benefited nor harmed. Therefore, this is commensalism and Assertion (A) is true.

In commensalism one species benefits and the other is neither benefited nor harmed; the barnacles are benefited. Hence Reason (R), stating that neither species benefits, is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Choose a correct option that shows an interaction in which one species benefits while the other is neither harmed nor benefitted.
options: Mycorrhizal associations between fungi and roots of higher plants
Abingdon tortoises and goats in the Galapagos Island
questions.solution:
An interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited is commensalism. The clownfish gets protection from predators among the stinging tentacles of the sea anemone, while the anemone is not affected.

Mycorrhiza is mutualism, the competition of tortoises and goats is interspecific competition, and Cuscuta on hedge plants is parasitism.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Competition is a type of interspecific interaction between two or more species when the resources necessary for them are limited and adversely affect them.

Reason (R) : Special adaptation may allow the competing species to coexist in the same geographical area.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Competition is an interspecific interaction in which the species are adversely affected when resources are limited, so the assertion is true. Special adaptations such as resource partitioning (for example Connell's barnacle study or MacArthur's warblers) may allow competing species to coexist, so the reason is true. However, coexistence does not explain what competition is, so the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth curve is sigmoid in nature.

Reason (R) : A population growing in a habitat with limited resources shows initially a lag phase, followed by phases of acceleration and deceleration and finally an asymptote.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: in the Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth model, the plot of population density against time is an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve.

Reason (R) is true: with limited resources a population first shows a lag phase, then acceleration and deceleration phases, and finally an asymptote when the density reaches the carrying capacity.

These phases together make the curve sigmoid, so (R) explains (A).

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: A biologist studied the population of rats in a granary. He found the average natality was 280, average mortality was 200, immigration was 40 and emigration was 50. The net increase in population is :
questions.solution:
Net increase =(+)−(+) .

=(280+40)−(200+50)=320−250=70

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: The population interaction where one species is harmed and the other is unaffected is :
questions.solution:
In amensalism, one species is harmed while the other is unaffected (for example, an antibiotic-secreting Penicillium harming bacteria).

In commensalism one species benefits and the other is unaffected, in parasitism one benefits and the other is harmed, and in predation the predator benefits while the prey is harmed.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Read the four statements given below and select the option having two correct statements :

(i) A lion eating a deer and a sparrow feeding on grains are ecologically similar in being consumers.

(ii) Predator starfish Pisaster helps in maintaining species diversity of some invertebrates.

(iii) Predators ultimately lead to extinction of prey species.

(iv) Production of chemicals nicotine and strychnine by plants are metabolic disorders.
questions.solution:
Statement (i) is correct: a lion and a sparrow both depend on other organisms for food, so both are consumers.

Statement (ii) is correct: the predator starfish Pisaster keeps the numerically dominant prey in check, so competitive exclusion does not occur and invertebrate diversity is maintained.

Statement (iii) is incorrect: predators regulate prey populations and normally do not exterminate them, since the prey would then be lost as food.

Statement (iv) is incorrect: nicotine and strychnine are secondary metabolites that protect plants against herbivores and are not metabolic disorders.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: The population growth curve applicable for a population growing in a geometric fashion, when the resources are not limiting in the habitat will be :
questions.solution:
When resources are unlimited, each individual reproduces at its full innate capacity and the population grows geometrically (exponentially):

dNdt=rN⇒Nt=N0ert

Population density therefore rises slowly at first and then ever faster with time, giving a J-shaped curve, as in (C).

The sigmoid curve (D) is logistic growth, in which density levels off at the carrying capacity K because resources are limited.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: The population growth curve applicable for a population growing in nature with limited resources available to them will be :
questions.solution:
In nature resources are limited, so a population shows logistic growth:

dNdt=rNK−NK

where K is the carrying capacity. The population first grows slowly (lag phase), then rapidly, and the growth rate falls as N approaches K , after which the density levels off at K .

A plot of population density against time is therefore a sigmoid (S-shaped) curve, as in graph (C). The J-shaped curve in (B) is exponential growth, possible only when resources are unlimited.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: The population growth curve applicable for a population of beetles growing in nature under unlimited resource conditions available to them will be :
questions.solution:
With unlimited resources every individual can realise its full innate potential to grow, so the population grows exponentially:

dNdt=rN⇒Nt=N0ert

The density rises slowly at first and then ever more steeply, so a plot of population density against time is a J-shaped curve, as in graph (C). The S-shaped curve in (B), levelling off at the carrying capacity, applies only when resources are limited.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : A given fig species can be pollinated only by its partner’ wasp.

Reason (R) : The wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for suitable egg laying sites.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Each fig species is pollinated by its own particular wasp species, so Assertion (A) is true.

The wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for suitable egg-laying sites, so Reason (R) is true. This is exactly why the wasp pollinates the fig, so (R) explains (A).

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : A cattle egret and grazing cattle in close association is a classic example of commensalism.

Reason (R) : As grazing cattle move through the field, they stir up and flush out insects from the vegetation that otherwise might be difficult for egrets to find and catch.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
In the association of a cattle egret with grazing cattle, the egret feeds on insects flushed out by the moving cattle, so the egret benefits while the cattle are neither benefited nor harmed. This is commensalism, so the Assertion is true.

The Reason is also true and states exactly how the egret benefits, hence it explains the Assertion.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: The status of the human population reflected in the human age pyramid given below is :
questions.solution:
The future growth of a population depends on how many individuals will enter the reproductive age group. In the given pyramid the pre-reproductive (bottom) bars are narrower than the reproductive bars, so fewer young individuals will replace the present reproductive group.

Such an urn-shaped pyramid represents a declining population. A broad-based triangular pyramid would show an expanding population, and a bell-shaped pyramid with nearly equal pre-reproductive and reproductive groups a stable one.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Cattle and goats are never seen browsing on Calotropis growing in abandoned fields.

Reason (R) : Cattle and goats avoid grazing on Calotropis because of the offensive smell of its flowers.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Calotropis produces poisonous cardiac glycosides, which is why cattle and goats avoid it. The assertion is true, but the reason (offensive smell of flowers) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Examples that show commensalism are :

(i) An orchid growing on mango tree

(ii) Cuckoo bird and crow

(iii) Cuscuta growing on Nerium tree

(iv) Barnacles growing on a whale
questions.solution:
Commensalism is an interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited.

(i) An orchid growing on a mango tree (epiphyte) and (iv) barnacles growing on a whale are commensalism.

(ii) Cuckoo and crow is brood parasitism, and (iii) Cuscuta on Nerium is parasitism; in both the host is harmed.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : A species of wasp and a fig species cannot complete their life cycle without each other.

Reason (R) : While visiting wasps come to lay eggs in the fig inflorescence, the flower of wasp gets pollinated in return.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion: a particular fig species is pollinated only by its own wasp species, and the wasp lays its eggs in the fig ovaries and the larvae develop there. Neither can complete its life cycle without the other, so the assertion is true.

Reason: the visiting wasp pollinates the fig flowers while laying eggs, and this is the return the fig receives for providing the brood site. It explains the mutual dependence stated in the assertion.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Darwin showed how even a slow growing animal like an elephant could reach enormous numbers.

Reason (R) : When resources in the habitat are unlimited, each species has the ability to realise its innate potential fully.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Darwin, using the elephant (the slowest breeder known) as an example, showed that even a slow-breeding species would produce enormous numbers in a few centuries, so the assertion is true.

Reason: when resources are unlimited, every species can realise its full biotic (innate) potential, which is true. This is the basis of the calculation for the elephant, so the reason explains the assertion.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Many copepods live on the body surface of marine fish. This relationship is an example of :
questions.solution:
Copepods live on the body surface of marine fish and feed on them, so the copepod benefits while the fish is harmed. Such an association, in which one species (the parasite) obtains nourishment from another (the host) and harms it, is parasitism. Here the copepods are ectoparasites.

Commensalism and mutualism involve no harm to the fish, and amensalism does not involve any benefit to the other species.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Interaction between clown fish living among the stinging tentacles of sea anemone is an example of –
questions.solution:
The clown fish lives among the stinging tentacles of the sea anemone and gets protection from predators. The anemone is neither harmed nor benefited by the fish.

An interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited is commensalism.

Amensalism and parasitism involve harm to one species, and mutualism requires benefit to both.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: A Tight one-to-one relationship between many species of fig tree and certain wasps is an example of -
questions.solution:
In the fig-wasp relationship each fig species is pollinated by its own species of wasp, and the wasp lays its eggs in the fig fruit and feeds on the developing seeds. Both partners benefit and depend on each other, which is mutualism. In commensalism one partner is unaffected, in parasitism one is harmed, and in amensalism one is harmed while the other is unaffected.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
Important attributes belonging to a population but not to an individual are :

(i) Birth rate and death rate
(ii) Male and female
(iii) Birth and death
(iv) Sex-ratio

Select the correct option from the given options :
questions.solution:
Birth rate, death rate and sex-ratio are statistical attributes that exist only for a group, so they belong to a population.

An individual is simply born, dies, and is either male or female; these are individual traits, not population attributes. Hence (ii) and (iii) are excluded.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
Assertion (A): The Monarch butterfly is highly distasteful to the predators.

Reason (R): The butterfly has a very rough skin which is not palatable.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion: the Monarch butterfly is highly distasteful to its predators, which is true.

Reason: it acquires a special chemical (cardiac glycoside) from the poisonous weed it feeds on as a caterpillar, and the chemical makes it unpalatable. Its skin is not rough, so the reason is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Identify the option that does not exhibit a parasitic relationship.
questions.solution:
A parasite lives on or in a host and obtains food from it, harming the host.

Head lice on humans, Cuscuta (a parasitic plant) on a mango tree and ticks on dogs are all parasites that depend on their hosts.

The female Anopheles is only a blood-sucking vector that takes a blood meal temporarily and does not live on a host, so it is not treated as a parasite (it is the host of the Plasmodium parasite).

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Assertion (A): The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys uses sexual deceit to get pollinated by a species of bee.

Reason (R): The female bee changes its colour depending on the temperature of the area.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys is pollinated by sexual deceit: one petal of its flower resembles the female bee in size, colour and markings, so the male bee pseudocopulates with the flower and pollinates it. Assertion (A) is true.

The resemblance is a fixed floral mimicry, evolved with the bee species; the female bee does not change its colour with temperature. Reason (R) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
